The profound insight of De Rham theory concerns the relationship between local differential information and global topological properties. It establishes that certain closed differential forms (those where $d\omega = 0$) are not necessarily exact (those where $\omega = d\eta$). These cohomology groups are invariant under smooth deformations (diffeomorphisms) and are isomorphic to the singular cohomology groups of the manifold with real coefficients. Essentially, De Rham theory translates topological questions about shapes and holes into analytical problems involving differential equations and integration, providing a powerful bridge between topology and analysis.

### 1. Core Architecture & Philosophy
*   **Set Prediction**: Unlike traditional models (like Faster R-CNN) that perform region proposal and then classify them, DETR predicts objects directly as a set $(p_i, \ell_i) \to P_i$, where $p_i$ are bounding box coordinates and $\ell_i$ are class logits.
